newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambique approves foreign bank credit.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique approves foreign bank credit.

text.p: Foreign institutions will in future be allowed to provide credit directly to Mozambican companies without going through local banks, according to the governor of Mozambique's central bank, Banco de Mocambique.
"Any citizen is authorised to contract loans abroad," governor Adriano Maleiane told Thursday's issue of the Maputo daily Mediafax.
"There's just a requirement to submit the terms and conditions of this credit to the foreign exchange control department of the central bank, for purposes of licensing and advice," he added.
Maleiane was reacting to local news reports this week that the U.S.-based Equator Bank was ready to offer credit at international interest rates.

Mozambican businesses will be able to borrow money from Equator in U.S. dollars at eight to nine percent interest compared with other banks who charge 44 to 46 percent interest for loans in the Mozambican currency, meticais.
The central bank has cut its rediscount rate twice in the past month, first from 54.75 to 48.75 per cent, and later to 40.75 per cent.
Maleiane said it was up to the productive business sector to put pressure on the commercial banks to cut rates, as they were doing by threatening to turn to Equator for credit.
